## GET /admin-api/applications

`getApplications`

**Every application this service has been asked about, filtered and paged**

The other side of /admin-api/users. That resource lists every identity that has authenticated here; this lists what they authenticated TO — every OAuth client, OpenID Connect relying party, SAML 2.0 or 1.1 service provider, WS-Federation application, WS-Trust relying party, OpenID4VP verifier and Kerberos service.

**The entries ARE the registry.** They live under `ou=applications` in the embedded LDAP directory and nothing caches them, so an `ldapmodify` is visible here on the next call — and changes what RFC 9700 mode enforces at the same moment. The RFC 7591 client registrations are those entries too.

**One entry per identifier, whatever protocol brought it.** The key is the identifier exactly as it arrived, so an application appearing under one name in two protocols is one row with two `kinds` rather than two rows.

`?application=<id>` returns ONE of them with every attribute of its directory entry and what the published schema says each attribute is; that reply pages its attribute list under `attributesPage` rather than `page`, which is the convention for a reply holding a list that is not the top-level one.

**The ?application= reply's `authenticationEvents`** (#954) are the audit log's authentication attempts that name this application, newest first: `authentication`, `authentication.refused`, `session.refuse` and `session.refused`, where `detail.client_id` or `detail.application` is the identifier or one of the entry's protocol names, exactly as spelled. Each row is an audit event. `authenticationEventsMatched` is how many, `authenticationEventsPaging` pages them under `authenticationsPage`, `authenticationEventsKnownActors` says which actors have a user page, and `authenticationEventsLog` says how full the audit log is. The member is not `authentications`: that one is the count. The list holds no more history than the audit log does, and nothing in it is a credential. Another process's rows are read before this reply is built, the same wait GET /admin-api/audit makes, so an attempt recorded on a different worker is on the list.

**The ?application= reply's `page.passkeyPolicies`** (#609, #1235) is what the console draws as the read-only Passkey policy card of the Every protocol sub-tab: the passkey policy the application names in `appPasskeyPolicy` (`named`; `default` for none), `missing` (true where the realm holds no policy of that name, so the default applies), `applies` and its `precedence` (what a sign-in for the application gets before any person is known), `groupPolicies` (how many named policies a group names, which could still win for a member on a lower precedence) and `link`.

**The ?application= reply's `credentials.stored`** (#1227) is what the entry stores in `userCertificate`, each certificate's SHA-256, subject, issuer, serial and validity, in the shape GET /admin-api/users/certificates lists a person's: an outside certificate authority's certificate authenticates the application only while it is stored there and on no other entry. POST /admin-api/applications/add-certificate and `remove-certificate` change it.

**This reply carries credentials** — `oauthClientSecret` and `appRegistrationAccessToken`, opened. They are sealed at rest wherever the process holds a durable key-encryption key, but anyone who can read this reply can authenticate as that client.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/applications` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `claimsUser` | query | string |  | On one application, the person the claims preview is drawn for. Defaults to the signed-in person. |
| `application` | query | string |  | One application, by its identifier exactly — the client_id, wtrealm, AppliesTo, entityID or service principal name. Answers 200 with `found: false` for one this service has never accepted, which is a different fact from one it has refused: an entry appears when an identifier is ACCEPTED, so a client whose every request was turned away has none. |
| `q` | query | string |  | Substring of the identifier or the name, case-insensitive. Ignored when `application` is given. |
| `kind` | query | one of `oauth2-client`, `oauth2-resource-server`, `oidc-relying-party`, `saml2-service-provider`, `saml11-relying-party`, `wsfed-relying-party`, `wstrust-relying-party`, `oid4vp-verifier`, `federation-identity-provider`, `kerberos-service`, `gnap-client`, `gnap-resource-server` |  | One kind. A record carrying SEVERAL matches on any of them — an OAuth client that asked for the openid scope is also a relying party — so these are not disjoint sets and the counts in the reply's `kinds` member do not sum to the total. |
| `exclude` | query | array |  | An identifier to leave out of the match, exactly as spelled; repeat it for several (`exclude=a&exclude=b`). Applied before the paging, so a page still holds `per` rows. The console's application search for `appAllowedToDelegateTo` and `appAllowedToActOnBehalfOf` sends the application itself and the values its list already holds. Ignored when `application` is given. |
| `attributesPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of the attribute list, on the `?application=` reply only. Named rather than the bare `page` because it moves a list inside the reply rather than the reply itself. |
| `authenticationsPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `authenticationEvents`, on the `?application=` reply only. Named rather than the bare `page` so it does not move the attribute list. |
| `page` | query | integer |  | Which page of the match to return. CLAMPED rather than refused: a page past the end returns the last one, and the reply says which page it actually is. |
| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 300. On a drill-down it is SHARED by every list in the reply, which each carry a page number of their own. |
| `observedPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `observed` to return, answered by `observedPaging`. On the `?application=` reply only: the claims observed on its tokens. |
| `heldPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `held` to return, answered by `heldPaging`. On the `?application=` reply only: the delegated permissions it holds. |
| `exposedPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `exposed` to return, answered by `exposedPaging`. On the `?application=` reply only: the permissions it exposes. |
| `grantedOutPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `grantedOut` to return, answered by `grantedOutPaging`. On the `?application=` reply only: the permissions it has granted out. |
| `enrolledPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `enrolled` to return, answered by `enrolledPaging`. On the `?application=` reply only: the certificates on its entry. |
| `enrolledConfigPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `enrolledConfig` to return, answered by `enrolledConfigPaging`. On the `?application=` reply only: those certificates on its configuration tab. |
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

`addApplicationValue`

**Add a value to a multi-valued attribute**

For the attributes that hold a LIST — `appCorsOrigin`, `appAllowedProtocol`, `oauthClientId`, `oauthAudience`, `oauthRedirectUri`, `oauthClaimsRedirectUri`, `oauthPostLogoutRedirectUri`, `oauthGrantType`, `oauthResponseType`, `oauthAllowedTokenResponseTypes`, `oauthScope`, `oauthAllowedScope`, `oauthPermission`, `oauthRoleGatedPermission`, `oauthDelegatedPermission`, `oauthGlobalConsent`, `oauthTokenEndpointAuthMethod`, `oauthRequestUri`, `oauthAuthorizationDetailsType`, `oauthAuthorizationDetailsTypes`, `authzenAttribute`, `appAuthzenApplication`, `appAuthzenCallbackUri`, `oauthAssertionIssuer`, `oauthSamlAssertionIssuer`, `oauthSoftwareStatementIssuer`, `samlEntityId`, `samlAssertionConsumerService`, `samlSingleLogoutService`, `samlSigningCertificate`, `oauthAccessTokenClaim`, `appRequiredRole`, `appAllowedToDelegateTo`, `appAllowedToActOnBehalfOf`, `appDelegationSubjectGroup`, `appDelegationSemantics`, `wsfedRealm`, `wsfedReplyUrl`, `wsfedSignOutUri`, `wstrustAppliesTo`, `wstrustJwtScope`, `krb5ServicePrincipalName`, `krb5S4uSelfRealm`, `oid4vpClientId`, `federationPartnerId`, `ldapBindDn`, `scimClientId`, `acmeAllowedProfiles`, `estAllowedProfiles`, `scepAllowedProfiles`, `didPublicKeyJwk`, `didService`, `didAlsoKnownAs`, `scimClientScopeGroups`, `scimClientGroups`, `scimClientCells`, `ssfReceiverId`, `ssfDeliveryEndpoint`, `ssfAllowedEvents`, `gnapFinishUri`, `gnapInteractionStartModes`, `gnapAllowedAccess`, `gnapResourceServerUri`, `spiffeWorkloadId`, `appFederationRelationship`.

## POST /admin-api/applications/add-certificate

`addApplicationCertificate`

**Store a certificate on an application's entry, so an outside certificate authority's certificate authenticates it**

Stores one X.509 certificate in the application's `userCertificate` (RFC 4523; written as `userCertificate;binary`). A certificate from an outside certificate authority — one trusted through the Client Truststores — is an identity at a door that reads a client certificate as an application (a Shared Signals receiver's, for one) only while it is stored, byte for byte, on exactly one entry of the realm: never by its common name or subject (#1061, #1227). Refused when it is not one certificate (STS-ADMIN-0897), when it is already stored on another entry (STS-ADMIN-0899) or the registry holds no such application (STS-ADMIN-0906). A renewed certificate is stored again. Sends a CAEP credential-change (x509) under the application's own subject. RFC 8705's token endpoint does not read it: `tls_client_auth` keeps its own registered subject.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `application` | string | yes | The application's identifier, exactly as this registry holds it. |
| `certificate` | string | yes | The leaf, as one PEM block or base64 DER. |

**200**: The certificates the entry stores now.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `application` | object, or string, or null |  |  |

## POST /admin-api/applications/add-owner

`addApplicationOwner`

**Add one owner to an application**

Adds a person or a group of this realm to the application's `appOwner` values and writes at once. `owner` is a username, a DN or a `urn:uuid:` subject for a person, a `cn` or DN for a group. One that names nobody is refused; at most 25. An owner already listed is `ok` with `changed: false`.

**AN OWNER GRANTS NOTHING**; the user portal lists what a person owns.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `application` | string | yes |  |
| `owner` | string | yes | The person or group to add. |

**200**: The application's owners as they now stand (`owners`).

## POST /admin-api/applications/add-secret

`addApplicationClientSecret`

**Add a client secret beside the ones an application holds**

Mints a secret as `regenerate-secret` does and ADDS it: every secret already held goes on authenticating until its own expiry. The new one is the newest, so it becomes the PRIMARY — the one this service signs HS256 ID Tokens and JARM with, keys symmetric encryption with, and returns as RFC 7591's `client_secret`. `lifetimeDays` is its lifetime in whole days, 0 to 730 (0 never expires; omitted or empty, `oauth2.clientSecretLifetimeDays`), and `description` one line saying what it is for. Refused past `oauth2.clientSecretsMax`.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `application` | string | yes |  |
| `description` | string |  |  |
| `lifetimeDays` | integer or string |  |  |

**200**: The new secret in `clientSecret`, its `secretId` and `expiresAt` (seconds, 0 never), and the application as it now stands.

## POST /admin-api/applications/clear-permission-claims

## POST /admin-api/applications/confirm-address

`confirmApplicationReturnAddress`

**Confirm a return address a development-mode request recorded**

A return address — a SAML ACS URL or `shire` on `samlAssertionConsumerService`, a WS-Federation `wreply` on `wsfedReplyUrl`, or a callback this service learnt for its own console or portal on `oauthRedirectUri` — that a request NAMED while the realm was in DEVELOPMENT mode is written onto the entry and MARKED on `appReturnAddressObserved` (`<attribute> <address>`). **PRODUCT mode refuses a marked address** exactly as it refuses one that is not on the entry, so a realm switched from development to product does not trust what development learnt.

This takes the mark OFF and keeps the address, so product believes it from the next request. An address that is not marked is REFUSED by name rather than confirmed silently — it is already registered, or it is not on the entry. `add` of the same address confirms it too, because an explicit write is a registration.

GET /admin-api/applications?application=… lists the marked addresses as `returnAddressesObserved`, each with `trusted` saying whether THIS realm's mode believes it. Addresses recorded before this service marked sightings carry no mark and cannot be told apart from registered ones.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `application` | string | yes | The identifier, exactly as the registry holds it. |
| `attribute` | one of `oauthRedirectUri`, `samlAssertionConsumerService`, `wsfedReplyUrl`, `gnapFinishUri` | yes | The return-address attribute the address is on. |
| `value` | string | yes | The address, exactly as the entry holds it. |

**200**: The application as it now stands, with the mark gone from `returnAddressesObserved`.

## POST /admin-api/applications/create

`createApplication`

**Put an application in the registry before it connects**

An entry usually appears because an identifier was ACCEPTED — a client_id at the token endpoint, a wtrealm on a sign-in response, an SPN on a TGS-REP. This is how to get one in ahead of that, which is what RFC 9700 mode needs if a client is to be judged against its OWN redirect URIs rather than against the `oauth2.redirectUris` setting.

It is created with zero counters and a description saying it was created by hand, so it cannot be mistaken for an application that turned up once and never came back. Give it its redirect URIs and grant types with `add` afterwards.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

This is where the per-protocol identifiers and the redirect URIs go — `oauthClientId`, `samlEntityId`, `wsfedRealm`, `krb5ServicePrincipalName`, `oauthRedirectUri`, `samlAssertionConsumerService`, `wsfedReplyUrl` and the rest. ## POST /admin-api/applications/discard-address

`discardApplicationReturnAddress`

**Discard a return address a development-mode request recorded**

The opposite answer to `confirm-address`: the address was recorded from a request in DEVELOPMENT mode and is NOT this application's, so the mark on `appReturnAddressObserved` AND the address itself are taken off the entry. Product mode then refuses it as an address that is not there; development records it again, marked, if a request names it again.

An address that is not marked is REFUSED rather than removed — discarding is not the door for taking a REGISTERED address off an entry, and `remove` is, which says so.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

## POST /admin-api/applications/export-ldif

`exportApplicationLdif`

**Export one application's entry as an LDIF file**

Answers the application's directory entry as an RFC 2849 LDIF document with one record: `ldif` (the text) and `files` (the same, named and base64, which the console saves). Its DECLARED attributes only — what an administrator configures, the key-pair certificates among them; nothing this service recorded about its use (counters, sightings, observed scopes and addresses). The DN is the entry's own; `import-ldif` creates the application in whichever realm it is called in.

**CREDENTIAL MATERIAL IS LEFT OUT BY DEFAULT** and named in `leftOut`. With `credentials` true the client secrets, the registration access token, the RFC 7523 and RFC 7522 private keys, the DID private keys, a secret destination's write credential and the GNAP shared key are written **UNENCRYPTED**: each sealed value is opened, because a file sealed under this process's key-encryption key opens nowhere else. Keep such a file as you would the secrets in it. A Kerberos service key, an enrollment key or challenge and a GNAP macaroon key are never exported: each is minted by its own subsystem and no import could write it. An audit row says whether credentials went with the file, never a value.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `application` | string | yes |  |
| `credentials` | boolean, or one of `true`, `false`, `on` |  | Include credential material, UNENCRYPTED. False when absent. |

**200**: `ldif`, `files` (one `.ldif`), the `attributes` written, `credentials`, and `leftOut`: the credential attributes not written.

## POST /admin-api/applications/fga-create-policy

`createApplicationFgaPolicy`

**Give an application its default fine-grained authorization policy**

Writes the `fga-default` policy (one rule permitting every detail) into `ou=policies` for an application that has none of its own — one registered by a client, seen in development mode, or whose policy could not be written when it was created — and names it in `appFgaPolicy`. An application that has one is answered with it, `created: false`. Refused (`STS-FGA-0024`) when `ou=policies` already holds `xacml.maxApplicationPolicies` applications' own policies, and (`STS-FGA-0008`) when it cannot be written.

## POST /admin-api/applications/fga-disable

## POST /admin-api/applications/fga-enable

`enableApplicationFga`

**Enforce an application's fine-grained authorization policy**

Sets `appFgaEnforced`: from the next request every RFC 9396 authorization detail of a type this application declares is decided by its own policy, at the authorization, PAR and token endpoints, and so is every AuthZEN evaluation whose resource resolves to it. The policy is created from `fga-default` first if it has none. Refused while a declared type is not covered (`STS-FGA-0018`, naming each type and its uncovered member paths, `*` for an open schema), while its policy is disabled (`STS-FGA-0006`) or does not parse (`STS-FGA-0007`), and for an application this realm does not hold (`STS-FGA-0009`). `failure` names which. Every enable, including one of an application that already enforces, also grants each holder of REMOTE_PEPS in the realm (the members of `roles.remotePepGroup`) membership of `roles.authzenPepGroup` and the application in its AuthZEN scope, where either is missing, so a remote PEP's edge PDP may forward evaluations about it. A holder that cannot be granted is listed with why (`STS-FGA-0025`) and does not fail the enable. Disabling removes nothing.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `application` | string | yes |  |

**200**: The `policy` it is decided by, `enforced: true`, and `peps`: the remote PEPs `granted` (with `member` and `scope` saying what was added), those that `held` both already, and those `failed`, each with `why` and `code`.

## POST /admin-api/applications/fga-reset-policy

`resetApplicationFgaPolicy`

**Reset an application's fine-grained authorization policy to the default**

Rewrites the document of the application's own policy from `fga-default`, under the same entry name, replacing every rule in it with one that permits every detail; its enabled flag is kept. Needs `confirm` (`STS-FGA-0020` without it), and refused (`STS-FGA-0021`) for an application with no policy of its own — use `fga-create-policy`.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `application` | string | yes |  |
| `confirm` | boolean, or one of `true`, `false`, `on` |  | The rewrite is meant. |

**200**: The `policy` rewritten.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `application` | object, or string, or null |  |  |
| `application.allowedProtocols` | list |  |  |

## POST /admin-api/applications/forget

`deleteApplication`

**Delete an application entry entirely**

THE ONE OPERATION HERE THAT LOSES A FACT, which is why it is separate from `revoke-registration` rather than something that one does as well. The entry goes and takes its counters, its sightings and its attributes with it — for a client_id somebody typed wrong, or a realm from a test that is over.

It will reappear, EMPTY, the next time that identifier is accepted by a protocol: this registry records what this service has seen, and it is still seeing.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

## POST /admin-api/applications/generate-did-key

`generateApplicationDidKey`

**Generate a key pair for an application's DID, publishing the public half**

For an application declared for the `did` family: generates an ES256 (default), ES384 or EdDSA key pair, adds the public JWK to `didPublicKeyJwk` — with `replace`, after taking the keys already there off — and answers the private key, as a JWK and as PKCS#8 PEM. **THIS REPLY IS THE ONLY PLACE THE PRIVATE KEY IS SHOWN**: this service publishes the public half in the DID document it advertises at `<base>/applications/<identifier>/did.json`, and keeps the private half SEALED in `didPrivateKeys` to sign the application's Domain Linkage Credentials (`sign-domain-linkage`). The application's DID is `did:web:<host>[:realm:<id>]:applications:<identifier>`. Refused (`STS-ADMIN-0837`) for an unknown application, one not declared for `did`, or another algorithm.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `algorithm` | one of `ES256`, `ES384`, `EdDSA` |  |  |
| `application` | string | yes |  |
| `replace` | boolean |  |  |

**200**: The DID, the verification method and the document's address; the public JWK; and the private key in `privateJwk` and `privateKeyPem`.

## POST /admin-api/applications/import-ldif

`importApplicationLdif`

**Create an application from an LDIF file**

Reads an RFC 2849 LDIF document holding ONE application record, as `export-ldif` writes it, and creates that application in the realm this is called in, through every check a create makes. **IT NEVER OVERWRITES**: an identifier already recorded here is refused, naming it.

Only declared attributes are taken; a record carrying what this service records about use (a counter, a sighting, an observed value) is refused, naming each, and so is one carrying an attribute outside the schema or a credential no import can write. Credential material in the file is sealed on the way in exactly as a typed value is; client secrets keep their ids and expiries. Give the document as `ldif` (its text), or as `file` (its name and text), which is how the console sends an uploaded file.

## POST /admin-api/applications/issue-signing-certificate

`issueApplicationSigningCertificate`

**Issue an application a message-signing certificate from this realm's CA**

Generates a key pair and certifies it from the realm's `message-signing` Issuing CA with `digitalSignature` only and `urn:sts:application:<identifier>` as its subjectAltName. A WS-Trust request whose WS-Security signature over the SOAP Body and Timestamp verifies under it authenticates the application as its requester; it signs nobody in over TLS (#521).

**THIS REPLY IS THE ONLY COPY OF THE PRIVATE KEY.** `files` holds a PKCS#12 (base64), an encrypted PKCS#8 PEM key and the PEM chain, all protected by `password`, which is neither stored nor audited. Refused past `pki.messageSigningCertificateMax` valid certificates (`STS-PKI-0220`), for a key algorithm outside `rsa-2048`, `rsa-3072`, `ec-p256`, `ec-p384`, for an application the registry does not hold (`STS-ADMIN-0904`), and in a realm with no certificate authority.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

## POST /admin-api/applications/issue-software-statement

`issueApplicationSoftwareStatement`

**Sign a software statement for an application, as this realm**

Signs an RFC 7591 section 2.3 software statement with this realm's key and writes it onto the entry as `oauthIssuedSoftwareStatement`, replacing the one before. The application is the software PUBLISHER: hand the statement to whoever ships the software, and a client presenting it at `POST /oauth2/register` is registered with the members it fixes — they take precedence over the registration's own JSON (section 3.1.1), and whatever the statement does not fix, the client chooses.

**WHAT IS SIGNED:** `metadata` (RFC 7591 client metadata, e.g. `redirect_uris`, `grant_types`, `token_endpoint_auth_method`), with `software_id` defaulting to the application's identifier; `iss` is the issuer this realm publishes at the address THIS REQUEST arrived on, `sub` the application, `iat`, a `jti`, and `exp` after `lifetimeSeconds` (`oauth2.softwareStatementLifetimeS` when omitted; 0 for none). The header is `typ: software-statement+jwt`, which is how this service tells its statements from its other JWTs. A JWT claim or a member only registration assigns (`client_id`, the secret, the registration access token) is refused, and so is an address a registration would refuse.

**IT IS A TRUSTED STATEMENT EVERYWHERE IN THIS REALM**: nothing has to be declared for it, and where `oauth2.softwareStatementOpensRegistration` is on it admits a client to an endpoint closed to everybody else (product mode with `oauth2.openRegistration` off). It stops verifying when it expires or when the realm's signing key is replaced — in development mode, every restart. NOT A SECRET: a statement ships with the software.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |

## POST /admin-api/applications/issue-tls-client-certificate

`issueApplicationTlsClientCertificate`

**Issue an application a TLS client certificate from this realm's CA**

Generates a key pair and certifies it from the realm's `tls-client` Issuing CA with `clientAuth`, the application's identifier as the common name and `urn:sts:application:<identifier>` as its subjectAltName — the name RFC 8705's IMPLICIT mapping reads, so the certificate authenticates the application under `tls_client_auth` with nothing registered, and every access token issued on a connection presenting it carries `cnf["x5t#S256"]`.

**THIS REPLY IS THE ONLY COPY OF THE PRIVATE KEY.** `files` holds a PKCS#12 (base64), an encrypted PKCS#8 PEM key and the PEM chain, all protected by `password`, which is neither stored nor audited. Refused past `pki.applicationTlsClientCertificateMax` valid certificates, for a key algorithm outside `rsa-2048`, `rsa-3072`, `ec-p256`, `ec-p384`, and in a realm with no certificate authority.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `application` | string | yes |  |
| `confirm` | string |  |  |
| `days` | integer |  |  |
| `keyAlg` | one of `rsa-2048`, `rsa-3072`, `ec-p256`, `ec-p384` |  |  |
| `label` | string |  |  |
| `password` | string | yes |  |

## POST /admin-api/applications/load-resource-metadata

`loadProtectedResourceMetadata`

**Read an RFC 9728 protected resource metadata document and answer with the application it describes**

Give ONE of `document` (the JSON, as text or as an object) or `url` (where it is published). It is parsed and checked, compared with this trust realm, and answered with `plan`: the application it describes — `name`, `oauthPermissionBaseUri` and `oauthAudience` from `resource`, one permission per `scopes_supported` value with the resource prefix taken off, a client_id generated at random, and `oauth2` as the declared family.

**IT CREATES NOTHING.** Create the application with `create`, passing those values in `fields` together with `oauthResourceMetadata` (the document, as JSON) and, where it was fetched, `oauthResourceMetadataUrl`. Every value may be changed first — this answer is a proposal.

`authorizationServers` compares the document's `authorization_servers` with the issuers this realm's authorization servers publish at the address this request arrived on: `allMatched` when every one is this realm's, `anyUnmatched` otherwise. A mismatch is reported and is NOT a refusal.

**A FETCH FOLLOWS THE OUTBOUND POLICY**: `federation.outbound` must be on, https with the certificate verified (#171), no redirect followed, `federation.maxResponseBytes` and `federation.outboundTimeoutMs`. In product mode the host may not resolve to a loopback, private, link-local or reserved address, and a document whose `resource` is not the identifier its well-known URL was built from (RFC 9728 section 3.3), or is not https, is refused; development mode reports both in `warnings` and answers. A malformed document is refused in both modes.

The console sends an uploaded document as `file` (its name and text); a JSON caller sends `document` instead.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `document` | string, or object |  | The protected resource metadata document, as JSON text or as a JSON object. |
| `file` | object |  | An uploaded document: its file name and its text, which is how the console sends the file it was given. |
| `file.name` | string |  |  |
| `file.text` | string | yes |  |
| `url` | string |  | Where the document is published, usually `https://<host>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource[/<path>]`. |

## GET /admin-api/applications/new

`getNewApplicationForm`

**The vocabulary a new application may be created with, and where it would land**

The eight KINDS and the fourteen PROTOCOL FAMILIES a create takes, each with what it means, the FIELDS the console's form is drawn from (`declarations` — the per-protocol identifiers and the redirect URIs, deduped by attribute and each naming the families it serves), plus the container DN a new entry would be created under and how many that container will hold.

**It creates nothing** — the create is `POST /admin-api/applications/create`. This is the list that call validates against, published so that a caller learns what it may send from the service rather than from a copy of the list in a document.

**The container is THIS REALM'S.** The embedded directory is per trust realm, so `/realm/acme/admin-api/applications/new` answers with acme's `ou=applications` and an application created there is invisible to every other realm — including in an `ldapsearch`, which reaches it only under that realm's base DN.

**Declaring a protocol family grants and refuses nothing.** No endpoint in this service reads `appAllowedProtocol`: an application declared for SAML 2.0 alone is still issued an access token. It is a record of intent on the entry, and it is deliberately not a permission — a service that refused a protocol would remove a test case rather than add one. The configuration that DOES take effect is in `editable`.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/applications/new` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |

| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

## POST /admin-api/applications/refresh-metadata

`refreshApplicationMetadata`

**Fetch this service provider's SAML metadata and consume it**

Dials the `samlSpMetadataUrl` ON THE ENTRY — never a URL in the request body — and CONSUMES the document exactly as `POST /admin-api/saml2/upload-metadata` does: its endpoints become REGISTERED return addresses, its signing certificates what its requests are verified against, its encryption certificate what an assertion is encrypted to, and its NameIDFormats, AuthnRequestsSigned and WantAssertionsSigned are applied. That operation lists what is refused.

IT IS THE ONLY OPERATION IN THIS API THAT MAKES AN OUTBOUND REQUEST, and the second surface in this service that makes one at all — federation is the other. The same refusals apply: https with the certificate verified (the three `federation.outbound…` transport settings, #171), a timeout of `federation.outboundTimeoutMs`, no redirects followed, and a size cap.

ISSUING NEVER FETCHES. This writes the certificate onto the entry and an assertion reads the entry, so no sign-in waits on somebody else's web server.

A FAILURE CHANGES NOTHING — not the document, not the certificate — so an application that was working does not stop working because a metadata host was down.

For ENCRYPTION the `use="encryption"` KeyDescriptor is taken, falling back to one with no `use` at all; a `use="signing"` descriptor is never an encryption key, and is registered as a signing certificate.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

## POST /admin-api/applications/regenerate-secret

`regenerateApplicationClientSecret`

**Mint a new client secret for an application, replacing every one it holds**

Mints `oauth2.registeredSecretBytes` random bytes, base64url — the way `POST /oauth2/register` mints one — as the application's ONLY secret, a record on `oauthClientSecret` expiring after `oauth2.clientSecretLifetimeDays` days (never at 0), and into the stored RFC 7591 registration document where there is one.

**EVERY SECRET IT HELD STOPS AUTHENTICATING AT ONCE**, wherever the token endpoint checks a secret (RFC 9700 mode, product mode). **THIS REPLY IS THE ONE PLACE THE NEW VALUE IS HANDED OUT BY THIS ACT** — the audit row names the attribute and never the value — though `GET /admin-api/applications?application=` reads the entry back for an `admin:read` token, as it always has.

`sts-api-client` is REFUSED while `adminApi.clientSecret` pins its secret: every token for this API is minted with that setting, and seeding never writes over an existing entry.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `application` | string | yes |  |

**200**: The new secret in `clientSecret`, its `secretId` and `expiresAt`, whether one was replaced, and the application as it now stands.

## POST /admin-api/applications/remove

`removeApplicationValue`

## POST /admin-api/applications/remove-access-type

## POST /admin-api/applications/remove-certificate

`removeApplicationCertificate`

**Take a stored certificate off an application's entry**

Removes one certificate from the application's `userCertificate`, named by the SHA-256 of its DER (as `credentials.stored` of GET /admin-api/applications?application= lists it). From then on it authenticates nobody (#1227). Refused for a SHA-256 the entry does not store (STS-ADMIN-0900) and for an application the registry does not hold (STS-ADMIN-0906).

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `application` | string | yes | The application's identifier, exactly as this registry holds it. |
| `sha256` | string | yes | The SHA-256 of the certificate's DER, hex. |

**200**: The certificates the entry stores now.

## POST /admin-api/applications/remove-custom-claim

`removeApplicationCustomClaim`

**Take one of an application's own custom claims or SAML attributes off**

Removes the application's row of that name from one of its claim sets. The realm's row of the same name, if there is one, is issued again. Refused (`STS-REG-0206`) for a name the application does not hold.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

## POST /admin-api/applications/remove-owner

`removeApplicationOwner`

**Take one owner off an application**

Takes one `appOwner` value off the application and writes at once (#604). `owner` is the DN as listed; one not listed is refused.

## POST /admin-api/applications/reveal-secret

`revealApplicationSecret`

**Hand back one credential of an application: a client secret by its id, the registration access token, or a sealed key by its attribute**

The one way to read a credential this registry holds: `GET /admin-api/applications` answers each secret's id and expiry and never its value. `secret` is a client secret's id (the ids are in the application's `credentials.clientSecret.secrets`), `registration-access-token`, or the attribute of a sealed credential the application holds: `oauthAssertionPrivateKey` or `oauthSamlAssertionPrivateKey` (the RFC 7523 and RFC 7522 signing keys `/admin-api/pki/issue` put there), `gnapSymmetricKey`, `gnapMacaroonKey`. It needs `admin:write` and writes an audit row naming what was revealed — never the value. Nothing is changed.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

## POST /admin-api/applications/revoke-registration

`revokeApplicationRegistration`

**Withdraw an RFC 7591 registration, keeping the entry**

RFC 7592's delete reached from here instead of from the client that holds the registration access token — the same function, so the outcome is the same one rather than a second reading of what "unregistered" means.

**The ENTRY stays**, with everything it had recorded; the `client_secret`, the registration access token and the registration document go. Losing that an application was ever here because its registration was withdrawn would be losing the fact rather than the configuration.

Afterwards RFC 9700 mode treats it as an unregistered, PUBLIC client: PKCE is required of it, its secret is no longer checked, and its redirect_uri is judged against the `oauth2.redirectUris` setting rather than against its own list.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `application` | string | yes |  |

**200**: The application as it now stands, with `registered` false.

## POST /admin-api/applications/revoke-signing-certificate

`revokeApplicationSigningCertificate`

**Revoke one of an application's message-signing certificates**

Revokes a certificate `issue-signing-certificate` issued to THIS application — a serial belonging to anybody else, or one of its TLS client certificates, matches nothing (`STS-PKI-0221`) — onto the Issuing CA's CRL and OCSP responder. A WS-Trust request signed with it is refused from then on.

## POST /admin-api/applications/revoke-tls-client-certificate

`revokeApplicationTlsClientCertificate`

**Revoke one of an application's TLS client certificates**

Revokes a certificate `issue-tls-client-certificate` issued to THIS application — a serial belonging to anybody else matches nothing — onto the Issuing CA's CRL and OCSP responder. The certificate stops authenticating the application at the token endpoint at once. An access token already bound to it stays usable until it expires: a resource server checks the binding, not revocation (RFC 8705 section 6.2).

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

## POST /admin-api/applications/rotate-secret

`rotateApplicationClientSecret`

**Add a new client secret, keeping the others working for an overlap**

Adds a new secret, as `add-secret` does with the default lifetime, and moves every UNEXPIRED secret the application holds to expire when `oauth2.clientSecretOverlapS` has passed (a week by default; an earlier expiry is kept), so the client can change over without an outage. The scheduler job `oauth2.client-secret-expiry` removes them after. With the overlap at 0 it is a regeneration. Refused past `oauth2.clientSecretsMax`.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `application` | string | yes |  |

**200**: The new secret in `clientSecret`, and `overlapUntil`: when the old ones stop working (ms).

## POST /admin-api/applications/set-access-type

`setApplicationAccessType`

**Declare or replace an access type a resource application owns**

Writes one `oauthAuthorizationDetailsType` value from named fields — the access-type catalogue read by RFC 9396 authorization_details and by GNAP access rights alike — replacing the application's definition of the same `type`. A list field is an array or text with one value per line (`requiredMembers` is the definition's `required`); `schema` and `limits` are JSON Schemas (`limits` a subset: type, properties, required, additionalProperties, items, enum, const, bounds, pattern, format). `bearer: false` makes a token carrying the type sender-constrained; `maxLifetimeS` caps it; `derivableFrom` names the types it may be derived from (RFC 9767 section 4); `introspectionClaims` the person's claims the application is told at introspection. `interaction` (always, default, never), `consentActions` and `acr` decide, for GNAP, whether the resource owner must be asked and how strongly signed in (#432 phase 6). A definition that does not read is refused (`STS-REG-0294`) and the one declared stays.

`xacml` (rows of `path`, `attributeId`, `category`, `dataType`, `multiplicity`) and `notForPolicy` are the type's fine-grained authorization mapping (#564), written whole here and a row at a time by `set-access-type-row`, `remove-access-type-row` and `set-not-for-policy`; on an application that enforces fine-grained authorization a definition leaving a member uncovered is refused (`STS-FGA-0019`).

## POST /admin-api/applications/set-access-type-row

`setApplicationAccessTypeRow`

**Map one member of an access type to an XACML attribute**

Adds to `type`'s `xacml` mapping the row for `path`, or replaces the row already mapping that path: the member of an RFC 9396 detail of the type that becomes the attribute `attributeId` when an application's fine-grained authorization policy decides it. `category` (resource by default), `dataType` (string by default) and `multiplicity` (single or bag) take AuthZEN's catalogue names or the XACML URIs. The row is read by the mapping's grammar before it is written, and refused (`STS-FGA-0023`, with `field` naming the member that was wrong) for a path that is not a member path or names `type` or a common data field, an identifier this service reserves for what it writes itself (`urn:sts:xacml:*`, subject-id, resource-id, action-id, the current-time attributes, or a bare directory name in a subject category), or a category, data type or multiplicity outside the set. On an application that enforces fine-grained authorization the write is also held to coverage (`STS-FGA-0019`).

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

| `description` | string |  |  |
| `multiplicity` | string |  |  |
| `path` | string | yes |  |
| `type` | string | yes |  |

**200**: The definition written, in `definition`.

## POST /admin-api/applications/set-claim-attributes

`setApplicationClaimAttributes`

**Set an application's own directory-attribute selection for a claim set or its credentials**

Writes the application's own selection of catalogue attributes for one set — `access_token`, `id_token`, `userinfo`, `saml2`, `saml11`, or `credential` (its OpenID4VCI credentials). HELD, IT REPLACES THE REALM'S SELECTION for that set: the realm's ticked attributes are not issued to this application, and an empty `attributes` issues none. The catalogue is the one `GET /admin-api/claims` lists. Refused (`STS-REG-0215`) for an attribute the catalogue does not hold, or a set whose protocol the application is not declared for.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `application` | string | yes |  |
| `attributes` | list | yes |  |
| `attributes[]` | string |  |  |
| `set` | one of `access_token`, `id_token`, `userinfo`, `saml2`, `saml11`, `credential` | yes |  |

**200**: The selection now held, in `attributes`.

## POST /admin-api/applications/set-claim-selections

`setApplicationClaimSelections`

**Set an application's access token, ID Token and UserInfo directory-attribute selections together, writing only the ones that changed**

The console's OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect claims table, a column per set. Each of `access_token`, `id_token` and `userinfo` that is sent is the whole list of catalogue attributes that set should carry. A set sent with exactly the selection in force is LEFT AS IT IS — the realm's, if the application was inheriting it — and a set that differs becomes the application's own selection, replacing the realm's for it, as `set-claim-attributes` writes one. A set not sent is not touched. Every set is checked before any is written. Refused (`STS-REG-0215`) for an attribute the catalogue does not hold, or an application not declared for OAuth 2.0 or OpenID Connect.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |

| `access_token` | list |  |  |

| `userinfo` | list |  |  |
| `userinfo[]` | string |  |  |

## POST /admin-api/applications/set-custom-claim

`setApplicationCustomClaim`

**Set one of an application's own custom claims or SAML attributes**

Adds a row to one of the application's own claim sets — `access_token`, `id_token`, `userinfo`, `saml2`, `saml11`, `kerberos-pac` (#493: added to a service ticket for one of its SPNs) or `gnap_access_token` (#1250: added to a jwt-signed GNAP access token and to the JWT inside a jwt-encrypted one; the protocol's own claims win, and groups, roles and the ticked catalogue are not added) — or replaces its row of the same name. At issuance the application's rows are ADDED to the realm's set and win by name. A row is a typed value (`value`, with `${placeholders}`) or a directory attribute of the person (`attribute`, with `multi` and, for the JSON sets including `gnap_access_token`, `type`); a SAML 2.0 row may carry `nameFormat`, a SAML 1.1 row `namespace`. Held to the realm's rules: a reserved name, an attribute that may not be released or an unknown type is refused (`STS-REG-0206`), as is a set whose protocol the application is not declared for.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| `nameFormat` | string |  |  |
| `namespace` | string |  |  |
| `set` | one of `access_token`, `id_token`, `userinfo`, `saml2`, `saml11`, `kerberos-pac`, `gnap_access_token` | yes |  |
| `type` | one of `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `json`, `int64`, `uint64` |  | The JSON type of an attribute row in the JSON sets, `gnap_access_token` among them; in `kerberos-pac` (#493) every row's PAC claim type, of string, int64, uint64 and boolean. |
| `value` | string |  |  |

**200**: The application's rows for that set after the change, in `claims`.

## POST /admin-api/applications/set-not-for-policy

`setApplicationAccessTypeNotForPolicy`

**Name the members of an access type its policy deliberately never sees**

Replaces `type`'s `notForPolicy` list: member paths a fine-grained authorization policy is never given, listed so that the type still counts as covered. An array, or text with one path per line or comma; empty clears the list. Refused (`STS-FGA-0023`) for a path the grammar does not read, or one a row maps; and (`STS-FGA-0019`) on an application that enforces fine-grained authorization when a member would be left uncovered.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

## POST /admin-api/applications/set-permission-claims

`setApplicationPermissionClaims`

**Map claims to one of a resource server's own scopes**

Writes the directory attributes, from the claim catalogue `GET /admin-api/claims` lists, that an access token addressed to this application carries when `permission` — one of the permissions it exposes (`oauthPermission`) — was GRANTED. Granting the permission is the grant of those claims, a standard OpenID Connect claim included. They join the resource server's declared claims and combine with the client's as `oauthAccessTokenClaimsCombine` says; on a token for several resource servers only what every one wants goes in. An empty `attributes` maps none. Refused (`STS-REG-0344`) for a permission it does not expose, an attribute the catalogue does not hold, or an application not declared for OAuth 2.0 or OpenID Connect.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `application` | string | yes |  |
| `attributes` | list | yes |  |

| `permission` | string | yes |  |

## POST /admin-api/applications/sign-domain-linkage

`signApplicationDomainLinkage`

**Sign the DID Configuration resource for one of an application's LinkedDomains origins**

The DIF Well-Known DID Configuration: one Domain Linkage Credential (JWT form), self-issued by the application's DID with credentialSubject `{ id, origin }`, signed with a key its DID document publishes whose private half this service kept (one `generate-did-key` made). Host `didConfiguration` at `https://<origin>/.well-known/did-configuration.json`. `origin` must be a `LinkedDomains` service in `didService`. Writes nothing. Refused (`STS-VC-0115`) for an application with no DID document, an origin it does not list, or no kept key.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `application` | string | yes |  |
| `origin` | string | yes |  |

**200**: The DID Configuration resource in `didConfiguration`, the DID, the origin, the signing key's kid, a file name and where to host it (`hostAt`).

## POST /admin-api/applications/update-fields

`updateApplicationFields`

**Set several attributes of an application at once**

What the Save button of an application's field grid on the console does. Each member of `fields` names an editable attribute and gives what it should hold: a single-valued attribute is SET (an empty string or array clears it), and a multi-valued one has the values not given removed and the values not yet held added — exactly `set`, `add` and `remove`, applied per attribute, so every rule those hold still holds. An attribute whose values did not change is not written. `protocols`, when given, replaces the declared protocol families, and is written first, so a family-scoped attribute may be set in the same call that declares its family.

What one attribute refuses does not undo another: the reply names what was saved (`changed`) and every refusal, and answers 400 when there was any.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/applications, POST /admin/applications/new, POST /admin/applications/edit and POST /admin/applications/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `application` | string | yes |  |
| `fields` | object |  |  |
| `present` | list |  | The fields the console's form drew, by attribute name, space or comma separated or as a list: each one is cleared when the form carries no value for it. |
| `present[]` | string |  |  |
| `protocols` | list |  |  |
| `protocols[]` | string |  |  |
| `protocolsPresent` | string or boolean |  | Set by the console's form, which draws the families as checkboxes: `protocols` is then the whole list, and none ticked means none. |

**200**: The attributes saved (`changed`) and the application as it now stands.
